items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I wasn’t into Kenton, but I thought it was marvelous that finally somebody’s getting closer to the shores.

ctx.x: So was your jazz learning mostly from records?
Mostly from records, because we didn’t get American musicians coming to England at the time when I was growing up, because there was a musician’s union ban I think on © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

both sides. Certainly the English musician’s union didn’t want American artists coming in, like jazz musicians, because they said it would take work away from the local musicians. Well in a sense that’s probably true, but also, we couldn’t get to hear these wonderful people who were still playing. And I bitterly regretted it because they were over in Paris.
